# Scan a self-hosted model for prompt-injection resistance {#recipe-garak-llm01}

**Tool:** [garak](https://docs.kailash.tools/reference/garak.html) ·
**Section:** Scanning · **Level:** easy · **Time:** minutes (scoped) to
hours (full) · **Layer/Category:** ATTACK / A-2 · **Tags:** scan,
llm01, prompt-injection, garak

## Problem

You run a model on your own infrastructure — a local Ollama server, a
vLLM endpoint, a HF checkpoint on a lab box — and you need to know:
*can it be jailbroken or prompt-injected?* You want a reproducible,
reportable answer for the OWASP LLM01 class specifically, not a
one-off chat-and-see impression, and you want the run cheap enough to
repeat after every model or config change.

## Solution

Point garak at the model and scope the run to the LLM01-tagged probes:

```bash
# 1. (Kailash) tool is packaged under ATTACK/A-2 — confirm availability
garak --version

# 2. Scope it: list the probes you are about to pay for, before running
garak --list_probes -v --spec tag:owasp:llm01

# 3. Run the scoped scan against a local Ollama endpoint
garak --target_type ollama --target_name llama3.2:latest \
      --spec tag:owasp:llm01 -g 5 -s 42

# 4. Read the result
garak --report <run-report>.jsonl
```

What success looks like:

- the run prints its banner (`garak … v…`), then
  `📜 reporting to <file>` — that JSONL file is the deliverable
- each probe prints a progress line and a final score per detector;
  scores are per-probe pass/fail fractions
- the JSONL report carries every attempt with a `status` field; the
  hit log lists attempts that yielded a vulnerability
- rerunning with the same `-s` seed reproduces the same
  probe/target interaction set — diff two reports after a config
  change to see what moved

Expected output shape (abridged):

```
garak LLM safety & security scanning tool v<version> ( https://github.com/NVIDIA/garak ) at <ISO timestamp>
📜 reporting to garak_<timestamp>.jsonl
...
🔍 probing <probe> (<n> generation(s))
   <detector>  passed  <n>/<m>
```

## Discussion

- **Why `--spec` and not the full run:** a default garak run is the
  whole probe catalogue — minutes-to-hours per model and mostly noise
  when the question is specifically injection/jailbreak resistance.
  The unified spec grammar (`tag:owasp:llm01`) selects exactly the
  probes tagged to that OWASP class. Drop the `--spec` for the full
  baseline before an assessment is signed off.
- **Why `-g 5`:** five generations per prompt keeps a scoped run quick
  while giving detectors multiple samples. Raise `--generations` for
  higher confidence on a gated model; raise `--parallel_attempts`
  (e.g. 16) when targeting a hosted/local API that tolerates parallel
  load — garak hints at this when the generator is parallel-capable.
- **Why `-s 42`:** seeds make the scan a regression test. The workflow
  this recipe enables is: scan → change something (system prompt,
  guardrail config, model revision) → re-scan with the same seed →
  diff the reports.
- **The endpoint is the target, not the tool:** run the server on
  `127.0.0.1` on a lab box, as you would for any attack-surface test.
  garak drives the model hard with adversarial prompts by design —
  that is its job — so never point it at a production endpoint you do
  not own.
- **Reports are the handoff:** convert with `--report` to AVID reports
  for anything that must survive into a ticket or an assessment.
- **Scope discipline:** this recipe covers LLM01 only.
  Data-leakage/PII exposure is `tag:owasp:llm02`, hallucination
  behaviour has its own families — add one tag per question you
  actually have, and keep each run tied to one question.
